review_notes: I read the whole file and checked for repeated nontrivial reasoning. The main candidate is the "cancel a unit scalar from a submodule membership" argument. It appears twice, in t_smul_dQ_mem_scaledLattice and t_smul_dt_mem, each time as a manual hmem / hinv / smul_mem block. Mathlib already has Submodule.smul_mem_iff_of_isUnit, which I confirmed in Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Defs.lean, so no new shared lemma is needed. The three `field_simp; ring` branches in scaledDifferential_eq are short calculations, so I did not report them. The repeated unit-cancellation is small, and I did not compile the suggested rewrite. The other proofs share no repeated machinery that clears the bar.

findings.excerpt:
have hinv : D.t • d (algebraMap V F (D.Q j)) =
      (↑D.u_unit.unit⁻¹ : V) • ((D.u * D.t) • d (algebraMap V F (D.Q j))) := by
    rw [smul_smul, ← mul_assoc, Units.inv_mul_of_eq D.u_unit.unit_spec, one_mul]
  rw [hinv]
  exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ hmem
findings.problem: Both step (i) and step (ii) show that `x` lies in a submodule from `r • x ∈ S` with `r` a unit. Each builds an explicit `hinv` equation with `unit⁻¹`, rewrites with `Units.inv_mul_of_eq`, and then applies `smul_mem`. The second copy is at lines 258–262. The two blocks differ only in the unit and the submodule. Mathlib has `Submodule.smul_mem_iff_of_isUnit`, which does this cancellation, so the hand-written inverse bookkeeping is duplicated machinery.
findings.proposed_change: Drop both `hinv` blocks and finish each proof with the Mathlib lemma. Step (i) ends with `exact (Submodule.smul_mem_iff_of_isUnit _ D.u_unit).1 hmem`, noting that `hmem` is about `(D.u * D.t) • …`. To match `u • (t • x)`, first rewrite with `mul_smul`, or state `hid` as `D.u • (D.t • d …) = …`. Step (ii) ends with `exact (Submodule.smul_mem_iff_of_isUnit _ hunit).1 (by rwa [← mul_smul] at hmem)`, or restate `hid` and `hmem` with the nested `(a*u) • (t • _)` form. Neither proof needs the `Units.inv_mul_of_eq` computation any more.
findings.benefit: Each proof loses about four lines of unit bookkeeping. Both steps then use the same standard lemma for unit cancellation, so the repeated argument is stated once in Mathlib and a reader sees the intent immediately.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma smul_mem_iff_of_isUnit (hr : IsUnit r) :
    r • x ∈ p ↔ x ∈ p
